title: nutty silky Japanese solo-dinner Sushi
description: A comforting Okinawan-inspired solo-dinner dish made with 00-flour, featuring a nutty and silky texture, ideal for a Buddhist-temple-friendly meal.
instructions: Combine 00 flour, aquafaba, and flaxseed in a bowl to create a sticky dough.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes, until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Shape the dough into a ball and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Gradually add almond milk, matcha powder, sesame oil, water, dried seaweed, silken tofu, sesame seeds, toasted oat flour, and salt to the dough, kneading until a smooth and silky texture is achieved.
Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces and shape each piece into a ball.
Roll out each ball of dough into a thin sheet using a rolling pin.
Place a sheet of parchment paper on a flat surface and sprinkle some toasted oat flour on it, then place a sheet of dough on it.
Spread a thin layer of sesame oil on the dough and sprinkle some sesame seeds on top.
Roll up the dough and cut it into thin slices.
Serve the sushi slices with a side of steamed rice, if desired.
Refrigerate any leftover sushi for up to 2 days and reheat it in the microwave or oven when needed.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and cook the sushi slices for 2-3 minutes on each side, until lightly browned and crispy.
